analyst_view.overall: Lyon are 13th with 7 points and need a win to push into the top eight; Lillestrom are 34th with 1 point and close to elimination after a 1-0 loss at Plzen. Lyon have a new coach: Paulo Fonseca left for Sporting and Carlos Vicens, a former Guardiola assistant, started with a 1-0 win at Lille on Saturday, so this is his first home game; the numbers know nothing about the change. Lyon's injury list is long and not on the numbers' list, including striker Lois Openda (fractured fibula), Pavel Sulc, Tyler Morton and Tanner Tessmann, which helps explain only 4 goals in their last six. Lyon host Monaco on Sunday, so some rotation is possible. No match preview or referee was out yet, so this rests on the latest club news.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, 2.3 of them for Lyon, with only a small cut for their poor recent scoring. I lean lower, to about 2.9, because Openda, Sulc and other attackers are out and the numbers list no absences; Vicens's first game was a tight 1-0 built on defending the lead.

corners.text: The numbers say 12.0 corners, already up for Lyon's 38 corners in their last six. Lillestrom are likely to defend deep, and a new possession-minded coach does not change that picture, so I stay at 12.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, close to neutral after small form tweaks. Lillestrom's loss at Plzen got heated late, but a one-sided game at Lyon usually stays calm, and no referee is named yet, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.1 shots, already up a little for Lyon's recent shooting. With several attackers injured and rotation possible before Monaco, I shade it to about 28.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.5 shots on target, already raised about 6% because Lillestrom concede many on target. Without Openda the finishing has been weak (4 goals in six), so I go a little lower, to about 11.0.
